title: "Quick apply" is a multi-step chat (CV → name → email → archetype → lane → skills → GitHub → KO×1-3) — short but longer than a 'couple of minutes' on mobile
expected: A quick apply she finishes in a few steps on her phone, no account wall, no bait-and-switch length.
got: The conversational script (app/_lib/apply.ts:99-247) builds ~7 base steps plus 1-3 job-derived knockout questions; CV/GitHub are skippable and the lead-prefill path trims answered steps. No account wall, each step is one tap/short text, draft resumes on refresh. It is genuinely short, but the 'conversational' framing across 8-10 turns is more than the literal 'couple of minutes' she pictures — still far under a 20-field form.
l2_priority: Time the real mobile chat end-to-end against a seeded ČS job; count taps; confirm the archetype lane doesn't balloon for a retail applicant who picks 'experienced'. Verify no 'quick = 2 min' promise copy oversells it.
suggested_acceptance: On a seeded retail role, a first-time applicant completes apply in <= 10 discrete inputs and under ~3 minutes on a phone, with skippable CV/GitHub never gating submit.

title: Status link is minted on submit and shows the full received→hired timeline plus honest terminal not-selected/withdrawn states — the anti-ghosting she fears most
expected: See where she stands without emailing anyone; no silent rejection.
got: The accept POST returns a statusToken (app/api/apply/[id]/route.ts:487) and ConversationalApply renders a 'Track status' link immediately (ConversationalApply.tsx:443-450). /status/[token] renders the timeline with a 'now' line and dedicated not_selected/withdrawn cards (status/[token]/page.tsx:77-116; application-status.ts:38-47) — a company-side close reads as not_selected, never silence.
l2_priority: Open the minted status token live; confirm the stage shown matches the recruiter pipeline and that a rejection flips the page to the not-selected card (not a stuck timeline).
suggested_acceptance: A submitted application yields a working /status token that reflects the live stage and shows an honest terminal card on rejection/decline.

title: AI-use disclosure is shown before submit, states 'AI assists, a human decides' + the GDPR retention line, and is genuinely refusable — no pre-ticked trap
expected: An AI-use disclosure in plain Czech, before AI touches her, genuinely refusable, no dark pattern.
got: AiDisclosure mounts with showDataConsent on the apply surface (ConversationalApply.tsx:601), stating AI assists / human decides + the data-processing & retention statement (AiDisclosure.tsx:24-29). Submitting IS the consent, recorded with a 365-day TTL (consent.ts:10; route.ts:448 recordEntryConsent). No checkbox is pre-ticked because there is no checkbox to trick — consent is the deliberate act of submitting, with an erasure footer in every comm (comms.dataFooter, cs.json:150).
l2_priority: Confirm the Czech disclosure copy renders in cs (not English) and reads as plain language a non-technical retail applicant understands; confirm the erasure link in the ack email resolves to /data/[token].
suggested_acceptance: The apply page shows a Czech AI + GDPR disclosure above the action, with a working erasure path, and no pre-checked consent control.

title: Outbound Czech comms read as a competent human at the bank — warm 'Dobý den {name}', proper sign-offs, an encouraging early-career rejection line, no machine-translation tells
expected: Comms that read like a person at the bank wrote them, not robotic or auto-translated Czech.
got: Acknowledgement, rejection, schedule-invite, interview-invite and onboarding templates (cs.json:151-203) are idiomatic Czech with natural register and sign-offs ('S pozdravem, Náborový tým'). Rejection is deterministic so it never ghosts (comms-dispatch.ts:189-200) and gives early-career archetypes an encouraging line (rejection.early). This clears her senior-quality-on-comms bar at L1.
l2_priority: ACTUAL prose quality is L2's to confirm live: render each comm with real seeded values and re-read as a native Czech speaker — catch any interpolation that breaks the register (e.g. a role name that doesn't decline grammatically).
suggested_acceptance: Every candidate-facing Czech comm renders with correct grammar/register on a real entry and reads as bank-human, not auto-translated.

title: A real candidate session only carries grounded questions if session.instructions were pre-populated; otherwise /connect falls back to generic defaultInterviewerInstructions
expected: The AI first-round references this role/candidate, not generic small-talk — senior-quality on the screen.
got: /api/interview/connect uses session0.instructions || defaultInterviewerInstructions({role}) (connect/route.ts:117-119). groundedPrompt is sent only when session.mode === 'candidate' (:151). So grounding depends entirely on the recruiter-side session being created WITH grounded instructions; a candidate session whose instructions are empty degrades to role-name-only defaults. From Tereza's seat this is invisible, but it is the 'good machinery fed thin context' risk the rubric targets — minor at L1 because the candidate-mode path CAN be grounded; whether it IS, is a seeding/L2 question.
l2_priority: Run a REAL candidate-token session (not the lab) and assert the agent's questions name this role/candidate; confirm the recruiter create-session path populates grounded instructions (CV/JD/comp), not just a role label.
suggested_acceptance: A candidate-token interview session asks role-specific questions grounded in the entry's CV/JD, never generic small-talk.

title: Voice consent is an unchecked checkbox gating Start AND enforced server-side before credentials are minted; honest completed/expired/revoked cards, never a dead Start button
expected: Consent before the AI talks to her, genuinely refusable; a human still decides; no broken call on a dead link.
got: consent starts false (VoiceInterview.tsx:91), Start is disabled until checked (:693), and /connect refuses without it server-side (connect/route.ts:137-139 CONSENT_REQUIRED_ERROR). The portal shows ShieldCheck 'human decides' chips (interview/[token]/page.tsx:60-65) + AiDisclosure. Completed/revoked/expired render closed cards, not a broken call (page.tsx:26-46). Single-use + terminal-entry + denial-of-wallet guards are server-side (connect/route.ts:70-98).
l2_priority: Confirm the cs consent copy + 'human decides' chips render in Czech, the unticked box truly blocks Start, and the duration chip shows the grounded run-of-show length (not a hardcoded 5 min).
suggested_acceptance: The interview portal blocks Start until consent is ticked, refuses connect server-side without it, and shows a truthful duration + honest closed cards.

title: On the offer page itself, Accept lands on 'Náš personální tým se vám brzy ozve' with NO link to the onboarding next-step — the dead-end she explicitly fears; the next step only arrives by email
expected: Accept on /offer/[token] lands on a concrete onboarding next-step, not a 'People team will be in touch' dead-end.
got: The accepted card renders acceptedTitle + acceptedBodyCompany = 'Vítejte ve společnosti {company}! Náš personální tým se vám brzy ozěe...' (offer/[token]/page.tsx:194-200; cs.json:485-487) and STOPS — no inline link to /onboarding/[token]. The onboarding token IS minted (the offer token doubles as it: offer-finalize.ts:108-110) and a SEPARATE email carries the link (comms-dispatch.ts:362-365; cs.json:200-203). But on the accept page she sees exactly the 'we'll be in touch then silence' copy that is her core pet peeve; she must leave and check email to find the concrete step that already exists at the same token. One inline <a href={`/onboarding/${token}`}> would close it.
l2_priority: Accept a real offer token live; confirm the accept page shows NO onward link (only the 'HR will be in touch' copy) and that the next step is reachable only via the email. Confirm /onboarding/{sameToken} opens a populated questionnaire.
suggested_acceptance: After Accept, the offer page itself renders a visible 'Start your onboarding' link to /onboarding/[token] — the concrete next step is on-page, not email-only.

title: /onboarding/[token] IS a real concrete next step — a Czech pre-boarding questionnaire that saves back to the recruiter hand-off — reachable on the same token the accept mints
expected: A real onboarding next step, not a dead-end 'congrats'.
got: The onboarding page renders a localized pre-boarding questionnaire (preferred name, start-date confirm, etc.) keyed to the server's ENTRY_QUESTIONNAIRE_FIELDS (onboarding/[token]/page.tsx:21-28,144-184), POSTs to /api/onboarding/candidate/[token], and the accept starts the onboarding run so it surfaces on the recruiter tab (offer-finalize.ts:96-110). The dead-end is structurally fixed — the only gap is the missing on-page LINK to it (see tereza-offer-accept-deadend-onpage).
l2_priority: Open /onboarding/[token] live, submit the questionnaire, confirm answers land on Petra's onboarding hand-off tab and the entry reads Hired.
suggested_acceptance: The onboarding token opens a working Czech questionnaire whose answers reach the recruiter hand-off.

title: The offer card shows the entry's real company/role/salary/currency/deadline with a deliberate decline-confirm and a coral <48h countdown — reads as an official letter, reversible, no dark pattern
expected: A trustworthy offer with the real number; decline is deliberate, not a trap.
got: offerView pulls salary/currency/company from the real offer + job records (offer-finalize.ts:149-165); the card formats them per locale with a letterhead strip (offer/[token]/page.tsx:178-192,138). Decline routes through an alertdialog confirm with focus on the safe 'Go back' (offer/[token]/page.tsx:48-55,241-282); the deadline turns coral inside 48h (:220-231); an ambiguous POST reconciles the authoritative status (:88-101).
l2_priority: Confirm a seeded offer renders the real salary/currency (not blank/placeholder) and the countdown turns coral inside 48h in cs number formatting.
suggested_acceptance: The offer card shows the candidate's real offered comp and a reversible, confirm-gated decline.

title: Her status/interview/offer/onboarding legs are all token-gated and UNREACHABLE without a minted candidate-token fixture — the local mint path is the unresolved env open-question #3
expected: Tereza reaches /status, /interview, /offer, /onboarding via real tokenized links.

The DESIGNED experience is fully evaluable from code (this report), but L2 of all three journeys is unreachable until env.md open-question #3 (the clean local token mint path) is resolved. /apply/[id] is reachable with just an open job id; the status token is auto-minted by the apply submit itself, which is the one self-bootstrapping leg.
l2_priority: RESOLVE the token mint path before scheduling L2: confirm apply-submit yields a usable /status token end-to-end, and establish how to mint interview/offer/onboarding tokens locally (seed output / dev listing / recruiter-side create).
